summary.name: Yarn.social
summary.one_liner: Yarn.social is a decentralised micro-blogging ecosystem built on twtxt, where each user's posts are a plain text file they host themselves or get for free.
use_cases: Host your own micro-blog feed on a web server
Follow blogs and news sites in a social timeline
Get a free decentralised social feed without an account
Bridge Fediverse accounts into a twtxt timeline
Run a community social pod for a group
summary.what_it_does: Yarn.social is a set of open specifications, clients, servers and services built around twtxt, a format where each user's posts live in a plain text twtxt.txt file served over HTTP, one timestamped line per post. Users can claim a free nick on twtpub.com to get a hosted feed, or self-host a single-user feed with twtd (a Docker image) or run a multi-user community pod with yarnd. The twtxt.app web client is offline-first and can follow feeds by URL or nick@domain, and bridge services connect ActivityPub and RSS/Atom sources. The page states there is no algorithm: the timeline is just the feeds a user follows, in order.
notable: Posts are stored in a plain text twtxt.txt file the user owns and can move or back up
No algorithm; timeline is the followed feeds in chronological order
Components are open source under AGPLv3 and listed on awesome-selfhosted (MIT-licensed listing, Go)
Free hosted nick feeds at twtpub.com with no account needed
caveats: Platforms listed for clients like Yarn Desktop and community clients are named but their platform support is not detailed on the page
Hosted feeds are free per the page, but no limits or terms are stated
Client platforms beyond web and Docker server setup are not specified in detail
